test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A grocer marked his goods at 60% above their cost price and sold them at a discount of X%. If he gained 52% profit, then find the value of X.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive percentage formula: **Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100**.

Here, Markup (a) = 60%, Discount (b) = −X%, and Net Profit = 52%.

52 = 60 − X + (60 × −X) ÷ 100

52 − 60 = −X − 0.6X ⇒ −8 = −1.6X

X = 8 ÷ 1.6 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.
Formulas: **MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100** | **SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100** | **Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d304ef3607a0fef49a3f13d987c751699d15991af5c406c15353cc8d98d3e130.png] 
⇒ Given **Markup = 60%**, so **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 60 = 160.
⇒ Given **Profit = 52%**, so **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 52 = 152.
⇒ **Discount Amount** = MP − SP = 160 − 152 = 8.
⇒ **Discount% (X)** = (8 ÷ 160) × 100.
⇒ X = (1 ÷ 20) × 100 = 5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The price printed on an item is the **Marked Price (MP)**. Discount is always calculated on the MP to reach the **Selling Price (SP)**.

Markup Percentage

The extra price added to the **Cost Price (CP)** to set the MP is the markup. **Markup% = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100**.</p
